correctness.rationale: Positive axes are invariant by the coordinate factors. In the equation for M=u+v the dispersal terms sum to −δ(u−v)²; the resulting logistic upper bound gives global bounded trajectories with bounded derivatives. Logistic comparison for v gives liminf v≥v_0. At limsup times for v the derivative tends to zero, implying V≤v_0+aU for the two limsups. If U>0, its own fluctuation sequence then gives 0≤U[1/(m+U)−H]<0, so u→0 and the v equation gives v→v_0. For w=v−v_0−au the exact filter is w'=−(s+δ)vw−au'. Since u'/u→0, the initial memory decays after division by any fixed u^p, and u(t−τ)^p/u(t)^p→1 on each fixed lag. On a sufficiently late tail this ratio is at most exp(pητ), while the filter is bounded by exp(−(s−η)τ). For η<s/(p+1), dominated convergence gives w/u^p→−aL/s whenever u'/u^p→L. In the strict branch, p=1 gives w=o(u); hence u'/u²→−(H−1/m), and p=2 gives the lag limit. At equality, the exact per-capita drift is −H²u²/(1+Hu); p=1 and then p=2 give w=o(u²), so u'/u³→−H² and p=3 gives the cubic lag. Integrating the derivatives of u^-1 and u^-2 gives precisely the two reported amplitudes. Conclusions concern patch one and positive data only, not extinction of both patches. Frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected, not executed. The recorded symbolic and BDF checks are not needed to prove the global or infinite-time results.

evidence: For the exact ODE the proof of Thm. 2.7 uses g=1/(u²v²) and divergence (e−s)/(u²v²)−[1/((m+u)²v²)+δ/(u²v)+δ/(uv²)]. This is strictly negative at e=B for all m>0. The boundedness argument of Thm. 2.6 is independent of the strict inequality e>B.

The scalar lower comparison v'≥v[s−(s+δ)v] keeps the bounded omega-limit off v=0. If it stays interior, absence of positive equilibria would make it a periodic orbit by Poincaré–Bendixson, ruled out by the prior Dulac inequality. If it hits u=0, the logistic boundary flow puts (0,v_0) in it, and the prior one-sided local attraction gives convergence.

On the center graph the forward drifts are −(H−1/m)u² and −H²u³ at leading order, respectively, and graph invariance fixes the lag coefficients. The usual exponential transverse tracking does not change these coefficients, as positive u on a converging trajectory is subexponential (u'/u→0).
